text:
Casey: Quick retrospective — launch went mostly smooth, but we've got a growing tail of small regressions and a handful of customer-driven asks. Need to choose the 2-week focus: reliability patch wave or pull in a couple of UX/enhancement wins for paying customers?
Marta: Agree we should be surgical. What are the concrete deltas vs our SLOs?
Devon: Crash rate increased ~0.6% over last 24h (baseline ~0.1%). Embeddings route 95th latency +220ms on average. Batcher A/B still running.
Sam: Support has ~5 escalations from top-tier customers about "embedding instability" in last 48h. Also two asks for configurable cache TTLs (recurring ask but smaller immediate revenue).
Ajay: Two buckets: reliability (crash/latency) and experience (feature requests). My read: fix reliability first, but leave a fast path for any enhancement that unblocks expansion for a major account.
Casey: Proposal: triage items by (impact on SRE/customers) and (estimated dev-days). If an item is <=2 dev-days and hits >1 top-customer, include it in the patch. Bigger UX work goes into a scoped mini-epic for next sprint. Thoughts?
Marta: Sounds good. I'll pull quick dev estimates and risk flags.
Devon: Estimates: root cause (KV cache desync) = 3–4 dev-days. We can ship a guardrail (feature-flag) in ~0.5 day which should reduce incidents ~60%. Batcher latency fixes = incremental tweaks ~1–2 dev-days depending on A/B outcome.
Sam: TTL toggle backend ~2 dev-days + docs; full cache UI in console >8 dev-days.
Casey: Priorities then: 1) guardrail flag for cache desync (0.5d) 2) batcher latency mitigations (1–2d) 3) include TTL toggle in patch only if risk <=2d and QA green. Defer console UX to next sprint.
Ajay: I'll draft a short customer-facing note & changelog for transparency.
Marta: Owners: Devon -> guardrail + batcher tweaks; Sam -> TTL toggle risk assessment + support materials; Casey -> customer note + release PR; Marta -> coordination and rollout scheduling.
Devon: Starting a mini-branch now. Test matrix I'm adding to the PR:```
- unit tests around KV sync (new)
- e2e with small and large batcher workloads
- canary to 10% traffic for 1 hour
```
Sam: I'll add a support playbook snippet: recommended workaround, how to enable the guardrail flag, and escalation contacts.
planning-bot: NOTE: Proposed patch window Wed 10:00-12:00 PST. Reply with :thumbsup: to approve or suggest alternate.
Casey: :thumbsup: Wed works for me. Marta, can devs meet the canary window?
Marta: Confirmed — Devon and one backend engineer can cover.
Ajay: Draft customer note posted: https://redwood.internal/docs/postlaunch/4912345670-guardrail-note (will update before release).
Casey: Final checklist before patch: 1) tests green 2) canary 10% for 1h 3) support playbook ready 4) changelog + customer note. If green, ship and monitor 24h closely.
Devon: Will post canary results and logs here after the run.
Sam: Preparing the customer FAQ + support templated replies.
Casey: Thanks team — compact plan. We'll reconvene after canary and decide which enhancements to pull into the mini-epic for the next sprint.
planning-bot: ACTION: owners assigned: Devon=guardrail+batcher; Sam=TTL+support; Casey=note+release-PR; Marta=coordination. Deadline: 72h to initial canary.
